title: Island Runner: Load-validation harness and operational acceptance for dedicated throughput guarantees
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build and validate a reproducible, tenant-aware load testing harness (codename: Island Runner) and an associated acceptance protocol that customers can run or witness to certify Dedicated capacity throughput SLAs. This ticket covers harness implementation, benchmark methodology, acceptance criteria, telemetry requirements, and the operator/onboarding checklist for customer signoff.
background: Customers buying Dedicated want predictable throughput and guaranteed tail latency across realistic traffic shapes. Existing synthetic prober suites focus on uniform steady-state load and miss burstiness, mixed-tenant interference, cache-warm behavior, and autoscaler dynamics. Island Runner is intended to address these gaps with deterministic replay, tenant-mix simulation, burst fuzzing, and an operator-facing acceptance report.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run in two modes: synthetic-sweep and customer-replay; both produce deterministic reports reproducible across runs
End-to-end benchmark output includes: p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies, token/sec, GPU/CPU utilization, avg batch size, queue depth distribution, and KV cache hit rate
Can reproduce customer-provided replay within +/-5% of observed token/sec and +/-10% of p99 latency when run on identical Dedicated config
Automated pass/fail evaluation against SLA: sustained throughput >= committed RPS for 30-minute steady window and p99 latency <= SLA target under tenant mix profile
Operator runbook and customer-facing acceptance report are generated automatically (PDF + hosted dashboard link)
Security hygiene: replay sanitization pipeline removes PII and secrets before customer replays are executed in shared validation environments
test_plan: Phase A - Harness baseline: run synthetic-sweep across seq-len buckets [64,128,512] using single-tenant profiles
Phase B - Tenant-mix validation: run mixture scenarios (50/25/25 small/medium/large requests) to measure interference
Phase C - KV-cache warmup and cold-start: measure throughput/loss when cache is cold vs warmed with prefix replay
Phase D - Autoscaler fuzzing: introduce microbursts and measure reconvergence time and overshoot under different hysteresis settings
Phase E - Customer replay: run three anonymized customer traces through replay sanitizer and compare metrics to customer's observations
Phase F - Chaos gating: introduce controlled node drain and network blackhole for 60s to validate graceful degradation and fallback policies
metrics_and_instrumentation: Latency quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) per model-version and per-tenant
Throughput: tokens/sec, requests/sec, and effective batch size histogram
Resource signals: GPU util (SM%/mem%), CPU%, NIC saturation, PCIe stall counters
Queueing signals: incoming QPS, queue depth percentiles, request wait time distribution
KV cache metrics: hit rate, avg kv size, eviction rate
Autoscaler signals: scale decisions timeline, cooldown windows, replica counts, and allocation latency
Error signals: model OOMs, kernel fallbacks, 5xx rate, rate-limiter rejections

design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Deterministic seeding: Use deterministic RNG seeds to allow run-to-run comparability at cost of reducing variance seen in real traffic — chosen for certification reproducibility
Two-mode approach: synthetic mode trades fidelity for speed and safety; replay mode prioritizes fidelity but requires sanitization and stronger security controls

Autoscaler fuzzing: We will emulate real autoscaler noise by injecting jitter into load generators rather than altering autoscaler internals to avoid destabilizing production clusters during validation
Customer replay sanitization: Prefer conservative redaction (err on side of removing fields) which may slightly reduce fidelity but avoids accidental exposure of customer PII
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): Request to include cost delta and expected token-unit bill for acceptance report — added to metrics.
Security (Nina Patel): Must run customer replay in isolated VPC or ephemeral sandbox; added sanitization + ephemeral creds requirement.
Runtime team (Ravi Singh): Noted kernel fallback as primary cause of long tails at 512 seq — recommended per-model kernel profiling step.
Solutions Eng (Maya Lopez): Suggested including a short 'witness mode' where customer engineers can watch live run via limited dashboard access.
operator_runbook_excerpt: Step 1: Provision ephemeral validation pool matching customer's Dedicated SKU (document exact GPU type and node count)
Step 2: Upload sanitized customer replay or select synthetic profile and select tenant-mix template
Step 3: Run pre-checks: KV cache reset, baseline health checks (GPU temp, PCIe errors, driver version)
Step 4: Execute Island Runner; monitor realtime dashboard; abort on 5xx > 1% sustained for 2 minutes
Step 5: On completion, review automated acceptance report; if failed, capture traces and open follow-up with 'acceptance-failure' label
results_summary: Baseline synthetic runs show that the current Dedicated SKU meets committed steady-state throughput for seq=128 and seq=64 with p99 headroom of ~18%. Long-sequence (512) exhibits kernel-fallback driven p999 spikes under mixed-tenant scenarios and during autoscale oscillation. Replay runs with anonymized customer traces matched observed tokens/sec within 7% on identical configs; p99 delta was 11% (above our target).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Replay fidelity vs privacy — Mitigation: strict sanitizer + ephemeral sandbox + legal review
Risk: Autoscaler test destabilizes shared infra — Mitigation: run fuzzing only in isolated validation pools and cap max replica change rate
Risk: Long-sequence kernel fallbacks causing tail spikes — Mitigation: add model-specific kernel profiling and an auto-fallback to a lower-quantized variant during acceptance tests
